html:
The New River Shasta were a small Native American people of the upper New River and nearby Salmon River in the Trinity Alps of northern California. They spoke a Shastan language, related to that of the Shasta.

They may have numbered only a few hundred before contact. When gold miners poured into the New River country in the 1850s, they were wiped out within a few years, and their language survives only in a few short word lists. Their neighbours included the Tsnungwe and the Okwanuchu.
